title: Compactified graph maps of semilinear systems and their evaluation
statement:
Let $e:U\to T$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type of schemes and $e=pj$ a compactification with $j:U\hookrightarrow\overline U$ quasi-compact open and $p:\overline U\to T$ proper. Let $R_1\leftarrow R_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be any inverse sequence of commutative rings. On each small pro-etale site use constant ring sheaves and the category $\mathscr S_Z$ of strict semilinear module sections $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ and its ordinary derived category [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. Let $e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}$ be levelwise sheafification of the direct-sum presheaf $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{t:V\to U\,/T}M_n(V,t)$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], formed on the slice $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, which is identified with $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and its constant ring sheaves [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Then $e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}$ is exact, being levelwise the exact extension by zero [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. For every pro-etale $V\to T$ and lift $t:V\to U$, its graph $\Gamma_t:V\to\overline U\times_TV$ is open and closed. Every $m\in M_n(V,t)$ has a unique extension as a section of $j_!M_n$ on $\overline U\times_TV$ with value $m$ on $\Gamma_t$ and zero on its complement. Summing these extensions on the presheaf summands and sheafifying gives a module-sheaf map
$$G_{\bullet,M}:e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}M\longrightarrow p_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet}M.$$
This map is natural in $M$, commutes with all pro-etale restrictions and semilinear transitions, and induces
$$\Theta=\gamma_{p,j_!(-)}\circ Q(G_\bullet):De_{\Sigma!,\bullet}\longrightarrow Rp_{*,\bullet}j_{!,\bullet},$$
where $Q$ is localization of complexes and $\gamma$ is the canonical right-derived direct-image comparison. Under the simultaneous-operation evaluation isomorphisms of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], evaluation of $\Theta$ at $n$ is exactly $\gamma_{p,n,j_!(-)}Q(G_n)$, the same degreewise graph construction with coefficients $R_n$, as an equality of natural transformations on the ordinary derived category of systems. No flatness of the ring transitions is required.

proof.text: Use the ordinary data and named helper statements in [def-sp-semilinear-compactified-graph-data]. The etale map $e$ is flat and has open diagonal by [def-weil-etale-morphism] and [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. An open immersion induces isomorphisms on local rings, hence is flat by [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus $e$ is weakly etale by [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] to identify the slice site and its constant rings with those on $U$. The presheaf in the item is exactly [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf], so [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] makes its sheafification exact at each level. The semilinear system category has componentwise exactness by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; therefore the resulting system functor is exact once its transitions are specified below.

proof.text: Put $Z_V=\overline U\times_TV$ and $U_V=U\times_TV$. The map $U_V\to V$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits] and separated by [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change]. Its section $(t,1)$ is an open immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-section-clopen-immersion]. Since $U_V\to Z_V$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], the composite $s_t=(jt,1):V\to Z_V$ identifies $V$ with an open subscheme. The projection $Z_V\to V$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], hence separated by [def-weil-proper-morphism]; its section $s_t$ is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-section-separated-closed-immersion]. This proves that the compactified graph is clopen, including when $V$ is empty.

proof.text: Write $C_t=Z_V\setminus s_t(V)$ and $F_n=j_!M_n$. On the graph, the inverse of the open unit [lem-exc-proetale-open-unit], restricted along $t$, identifies $F_n(s_t(V))$ with $M_n(V,t)$. Restriction along this open uses the ring identification of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. Apply [lem-pur-clopen-ringed-module-gluing] to the two clopen components of $Z_V$, with the restriction of the constant $R_n$ sheaf from $\overline U$. Its section formula identifies $F_n(Z_V)$ with $F_n(s_t(V))\times F_n(C_t)$. Define $g_{n,V,t}(m)$ to be the section corresponding to $(m,0)$. The same formula proves both existence and uniqueness, without finite-ring or constructibility assumptions.

proof.text: For $a\in(R_n)_T(V)$, its image under the constant-ring structure map of [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations] restricts on $s_t(V)$ to the scalar acting on $M_n(V,t)$. Thus the pairs for $g_{n,V,t}(am)$ and $a g_{n,V,t}(m)$ are both $(am,0)$; additivity is checked in the same way. For $b:V'\to V$, the fibre-product equations give $(1_{\overline U}\times b)^{-1}s_t(V)=s_{tb}(V')$, with complementary preimage $C_{tb}$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Consequently restriction of $g_{n,V,t}(m)$ has pair $(m|_{V'},0)$, so equals $g_{n,V',tb}(m|_{V'})$. For a module morphism $h:M_n\to N_n$, applying $j_!h$ gives pair $(h(m),0)$, proving naturality by the uniqueness in step 3. These identities also hold for local, nonconstant sections of the constant ring sheaf.

proof.text:
Let $\alpha_n:M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$ be a transition. Open extension acts on such systems by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; denote its transition by $\beta_n:j_!M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}j_!M_n$. Its restriction on $U$ is $\alpha_n$, since the open units are natural. Applying $\beta_n$ to $g_{n+1,V,t}(m)$ therefore gives pair $(\alpha_n(m),0)$ and hence
$$\beta_n g_{n+1,V,t}(m)=g_{n,V,t}(\alpha_n(m)).$$
On the direct-sum presheaf the transition sends each summand by $\alpha_n$, with scalars restricted through $R_{n+1}\to R_n$. Thus the displayed equality supplies its compatibility with the graph map. The presheaf transition extends uniquely after sheafification by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], using the target with its restricted scalar action. Compositions of transitions agree because they do so on every summand. Only restriction of scalars, addition and zero occur, so no flatness is used.

proof.text: Sum $g_{n,V,t}$ over the finitely supported elements of the direct sum [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf]. By steps 3-4 this gives a module-presheaf map to $V\mapsto(j_!M_n)(Z_V)=(p_*j_!M_n)(V)$, the direct image of [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image]. Its target is a sheaf. The universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives a unique $G_{n,M}:e_{\Sigma!,n}M_n\to p_*j_!M_n$. Naturality, restrictions and the transition equation of step 5 pass through this universal property, yielding $G_{\bullet,M}$ on systems. Ordinary evaluation of this map is $G_n$ because both maps agree on each lift summand and factor through the same sheafification. The empty sum gives zero; overlapping graphs require no disjointness, since their sections are simply added.

proof.text:
Apply $G_\bullet$ termwise to complexes. For a complex $K$ set $P=j_{!,\bullet}K$ and define
$$\Theta_{QK}=\gamma_{p,P}\,Q(G_{\bullet,K}).$$
Here $Rp_{*,\bullet}$ and its canonical derived adjunction are supplied by [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], and $\gamma$ is the unit of the right-derived pair [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]; its K-injective hypothesis holds because $\mathscr S_{\overline U}$ and each level category are Grothendieck abelian [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections, lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective]. Exactness of $j_{!,\bullet}$ and $e_{\Sigma!,\bullet}$ makes the source and target functors invert quasi-isomorphisms. For any chain map the square for $\Theta$ commutes by naturality of $G$ and $\gamma$. For the inverse of a quasi-isomorphism its square follows by multiplying that square by the two inverses. Since derived morphisms are generated by chain maps and these inverses [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], this defines the required natural transformation on the ordinary unbounded derived category of systems.

proof.text:
We check equality of the evaluated maps, not faithfulness of derived evaluation. For any complex $P$, $\gamma_{p,P}:Qp_*P\to Rp_*QP$ has adjoint transpose $Q(\varepsilon^0_P)$, where $\varepsilon^0:p^*p_*\to1$ is the ordinary counit. Indeed choose a K-injective resolution $i:P\to I$ [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective], as in [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. The derived adjunction $p^*_\bullet\dashv Rp_{*,\bullet}$ is the one induced by the ordinary adjunction [def-sp-semilinear-constant-ring-operations, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections], i.e. the canonical one of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-square-derived-counit] applied with $r,s$ identities and $\beta$ the identity; its counit satisfies $\varepsilon^D_{QI}\circ Dp^*(\eta_I)=Q(\varepsilon^0_I)$, and likewise at each level $n$. Hence the transpose of $\gamma_{p,P}=Rp_*(Q(i))^{-1}\eta_IQ(p_*i)$ is $Q(i)^{-1}Q(\varepsilon^0_I)Q(p^*p_*i)=Q(\varepsilon^0_P)$, by counit naturality. That node says evaluation preserves these units, counits and adjunction transposes. Evaluating the displayed transpose therefore gives $Q(\varepsilon^0_{P_n})$, whose adjunct is precisely $\gamma_{p,n,P_n}$. Hence, under its specified operation isomorphisms,
$$e_n(\gamma_{p,P})=\gamma_{p,n,P_n},\qquad e_n(\Theta_{QK})=\gamma_{p,n,j_!K_n}Q(G_{n,K_n}).$$
The second identity uses step 6 and exact termwise evaluation. It is natural for chain maps, and thus for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms as in step 7, proving the stated equality of natural transformations on $D(\mathscr S_U)$. No assertion about evaluated K-injectives or equality detection by evaluations enters this argument.
